items.question: How does a mantra-deluded woman approach the practitioner?
premises: A woman comes to the practitioner.
She comes properly and directly.
She is deluded by the mantra.
items.inference: The mantra causes a deluded woman to approach the practitioner properly.
items.plain_english: O beloved, being deluded by the mantra, she properly comes to the practitioner.

items.question: What form should the practitioner visualize as his own self?
premises: The self is to be visualized.
It resembles a thousand risen suns.
It is red in color.
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize himself as red and radiant like a thousand risen suns.
items.plain_english: Thus one should visualize oneself as red, resembling a thousand risen suns.

items.question: What transformation results from practicing this gradual yogic method?
premises: The method is a gradual union.
The practitioner applies it himself.
The result is assuming Kandarpa's form.
items.inference: By this gradual yogic method, the practitioner himself becomes endowed with the form of Kandarpa.
items.plain_english: By this gradual yogic method, one oneself becomes endowed with the form of Kandarpa.

items.question: How must the practitioner's body be prepared during this ritual practice?
premises: All red offerings are employed.
Ritual seals accompany the practice.
The body is equipped accordingly.
items.inference: The practitioner’s body must be equipped with all red offerings and accompanied by ritual seals.
items.plain_english: And with all red offerings, accompanied by seals, his body is fully equipped.

items.question: What subservient outcome can be achieved over a wealthy person or king?
premises: The subject may be wealthy or a king.
The ritual produces subservience.
The subject becomes like a servant.
items.inference: Through this practice, even a wealthy person or a king becomes like a servant.
uncertainties: Whether 'sa' refers to the practitioner or the person brought under control is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: O goddess, he becomes like a servant, whether he is rich in wealth or even a king.

items.question: What ritual posture must the wise practitioner assume toward an unseen woman?
premises: The target woman is unseen.
The practitioner is wise.
He holds the yoni seal.
items.inference: The wise practitioner should hold the yoni seal when working upon an unseen woman.
items.plain_english: O great goddess, the wise one, holding the yoni seal, acts upon an unseen woman.

items.question: Which types of supernatural women can be drawn by this practice?
premises: The targets include a serpent maiden.
They include a celestial nymph or sky-moving woman.
They include a divine woman.
items.inference: The practice can attract serpent maidens, celestial nymphs, sky-moving women, or divine women.
items.plain_english: Whether a serpent maiden, a celestial nymph, a sky-moving woman, or a divine woman.

items.question: What physical state of passion is induced in the targeted woman?
premises: Passion arises from the god of love.
Heat and throbbing are produced.
The effect centers on her hip region.
items.inference: The targeted woman experiences throbbing heat of love in her hip region.
items.plain_english: Her hip region throbs with the heat born of the god of love.

items.question: What meditative union empowers this attraction of the desired woman?
premises: The practice involves meditation on the great desire-art.
It is performed as a yogic union.
The goddess praised by gods is addressed.
items.inference: Union through meditation on the great kāma-kalā empowers the attraction.
uncertainties: Exact technical sense of 'kāma-kalā' is tradition-specific.
items.plain_english: O goddess praised by the gods, this occurs through union with meditation on the great kāma-kalā.

items.question: How should sandal paste be prepared in the next ritual step?
premises: A new procedure begins.
Two parts of sandal are used.
They should be rubbed equally.
items.inference: The practitioner should rub two equal parts of sandal paste.
items.plain_english: Then, O goddess, one should rub two equal parts of sandal.

items.question: How many mantra repetitions are required to bring the target under control?
premises: The substance is empowered with mantra.
The empowerment uses one hundred and eight repetitions.
The goal is to bring the target under control.
items.inference: After empowering it with one hundred and eight mantra repetitions, one should bring the target under control.
items.plain_english: Having empowered it with one hundred and eight repetitions, one should bring the target under control.

items.question: What scope of control does the mantra practitioner gain over the target?
premises: The agent is a mantra practitioner.
The effect applies to all that belongs to the target.
All of it comes under control.
items.inference: The mantra practitioner brings all that belongs to the target under control.
items.plain_english: O supreme goddess, by the mantra practitioner all that is his comes under control.

items.question: Which ordinary substances can be used as vehicles for this subjugation rite?
premises: Milk and ghee may be used.
Powder, cloth, and camphor may be used.
These are suitable ritual vehicles.
items.inference: Various ordinary substances such as milk, ghee, powder, cloth, and camphor can serve in the rite.
items.plain_english: Milk, ghee, mere powder, cloth, and indeed camphor.

items.question: How broadly does the choice of ritual objects extend in this practice?
premises: Fruit or any other thing may be used.
The inclusion is open-ended.
All such things are encompassed.
items.inference: Any object whatsoever, including fruit or other things, may be used in the rite.
items.plain_english: Or fruit, or whatever thing at all, O supreme goddess, all of it.

items.question: Is there any doubt about the target becoming subject to control?
premises: The target becomes controllable.
The result is stated as certain.
No deliberation is to be made.
items.inference: The target certainly becomes controllable, and no doubt should be entertained.
items.plain_english: O goddess, he becomes subject to control; no deliberation should be made about this.

items.question: What certainty is claimed for the forceful attraction method taught here?
premises: This forceful attraction has been taught.
The teaching is given directly.
No other outcome is possible.
items.inference: The taught method of forceful attraction is declared to work without exception.
items.plain_english: This forceful attraction has been told to you; it cannot be otherwise.

items.question: How should the woman be visualized in terms of dress and ornamentation?
premises: She is richly dressed in charming adornment.
She is adorned with all ornaments.
The visualization emphasizes beauty and decoration.
items.inference: The woman should be visualized as beautifully dressed and adorned with all ornaments.
items.plain_english: She is richly dressed in charming adornment and adorned with all ornaments.

items.question: Where on the visualized body are the corresponding circles to be placed?
premises: Specific body points are named: forehead, throat, heart, navel.
Corresponding circles are associated with them.
These are placed in their respective locations.
items.inference: The corresponding circles are to be placed at her forehead, throat, heart, and navel regions.
uncertainties: Technical meaning of 'janmabhūmiṣu' in this ritual context is uncertain.
items.plain_english: Placed at her forehead, throat, heart, and navel, in those respective circle-locations.

items.question: Where should the syllable of Madana be inscribed on the body?
premises: The body has many joints.
The Madana syllable is the object to inscribe.
Inscription is to be done in all joints.
items.inference: The syllable of Madana should be inscribed in all the joints of the body.
items.plain_english: One should inscribe the syllable of Madana in all the joints of the body.

items.question: What identity and orientation must the practitioner assume before the rite?
premises: The practitioner faces the direction of the target.
The practitioner assumes the goddess's form.
This is done by oneself.
items.inference: The practitioner must face the target’s direction while assuming the form of the goddess.
items.plain_english: Facing her direction, having oneself become of the form of the goddess.

items.question: Into what kind of Madana-abode is the figure ritually placed?
premises: The figure is placed in the abode of Madana.
That abode is composed of moon and sun parts.
Placement is a deliberate ritual act.
items.inference: The figure is placed in the abode of Madana, which is constituted of moon and sun kalās.
uncertainties: Technical sense of 'kalā' here may be subtle-energy parts.
items.plain_english: Having placed her in the abode of Madana, which is made of the kalās of moon and sun.

items.question: What mental and emotional condition is induced in the targeted woman?
premises: Her mind is fixed on no other.
She wanders in love.
She becomes languid with passion.
items.inference: The targeted woman becomes single-minded, love-stricken, and languid with passion.
items.plain_english: She becomes single-minded, wandering in love, and languid with passion.

items.question: On which materials may the ritual diagram or inscription be prepared?
premises: Birch leaf is a possible surface.
Gold or silver leaf may be used.
Copper may also be used.
items.inference: The inscription may be prepared on birch, gold, silver, or copper surfaces.
uncertainties: 'tāmraje' likely refers to a copper plate or copper-born material.
items.plain_english: On birch leaf, on gold leaf, on silver leaf, or on copper.

items.question: How must the inscribed figure be completed with mantra and diagrammatic elements?
premises: The figure is endowed with the mātṛkā syllables.
It is adorned with a circle of one's own command.
This follows the same procedure.
items.inference: The inscribed figure must likewise be endowed with mātṛkā syllables and adorned with the circle of one's own command.
uncertainties: Exact technical meaning of 'svamājñā-cakra' is tradition-specific.
items.plain_english: Likewise, endowed with the mātṛkā and adorned with the circle of one's own command.
